'''Hamilton Heights''' is a neighborhood in the [[Upper Manhattan|northern part]] of [[Manhattan]] in [[New York City]].  It is the northernmost part of the [[West Harlem, Manhattan|West Harlem]] area, along with [[Manhattanville, Manhattan|Manhattanville]] and [[Morningside Heights, Manhattan|Morningside Heights]] to its south,<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.cb9m.org/district | access-date = March 31, 2020 | title = The District - Manhattan Community Board 9 | website = www.cb9m.org}}</ref> and it contains the sub-neighborhood and historic district of [[Sugar Hill, Manhattan|Sugar Hill]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=James |first=Davida Siwisa |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SQ73EAAAQBAJ |title=Hamilton Heights and Sugar Hill: Alexander Hamilton's Old Harlem Neighborhood Through the Centuries |date=2024 |publisher=Fordham University Press |isbn=978-1-5315-0614-8 |edition=1st |location=New York}}</ref> [[Washington Heights, Manhattan|Washington Heights]] lies to Hamilton Heights' north, and to its east is [[Harlem|Central Harlem]].<ref name="Citycyclopedia">{{cite enc-nyc|pages=519-520}}</ref>

Hamilton Heights is bounded by 135th Street to the south, [[Riverside Drive (Manhattan)|Riverside Drive]] to the west, [[155th Street (Manhattan)|155th Street]] to the north, and Edgecombe Avenue and [[St. Nicholas Avenue|Saint Nicholas Avenue]] to the east. The community derives its name from Founding Father [[Alexander Hamilton]], who lived the last two years of his life in what is now the [[Hamilton Grange National Memorial]], back when [[Upper Manhattan]] was mostly farmland.<ref name="Citycyclopedia"/>

Hamilton Heights is part of [[Manhattan Community Board 9|Manhattan Community District 9]], and its primary [[ZIP Code]]s are 10031, 10032, and 10039.<ref name="NYCPlanning"/> It is patrolled by the 30th Precinct of the [[New York City Police Department]].
